  "summary": "S1: Fact—deliver a small Python HTTP service where organisers create events with seat capacities and people reserve seats; the request grants delivery to the service, with no deployed target named. Fact—the repository is empty and this run covers intake only; implementation remains for a later stage. Assumption—the service is usable through a locally running HTTP API; its source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and any deployed outcome becomes visible only after release. Open interaction questions and recorded defaults: discovery must first establish any available runtime or workspace conventions before choosing the API and storage, which blocks those implementation choices; no team, channel, internal site, document, private repository, or owner was named as a source hint, and organiser and people are role descriptions rather than identified accounts. Unless discovery finds contrary evidence, default to anonymous actors, shared event and reservation state within one service process, and state lasting until that process ends; this rules out account-based permissions, cross-process sharing, and persistence across restarts. Default to publicly visible event availability and no personal reservation data; this rules out private reservations and identity-based access control. The reservation operation must respect capacity when requests overlap. Any sensitive locator discovered belongs only in an authorized private store, never in committed KNOWLEDGE/. S2: Fact—include tests demonstrating the requested event and reservation behavior; they become usable in the returned checkout and visible when run. Assumption—the test runner and exact cases follow Python conventions discovered during implementation."
}
